source.title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a countable complete lattice L whose Scott space Sigma L=(L, sigma(L)) is non-sober? Here sigma(L) is the Scott topology on the order L, and non-sober means that some irreducible closed subset of Sigma L is not the closure of a unique point.

evidence.quote: Question 3.3. ([32]) Is there a countable complete lattice that has a non-sober Scott topology?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a complete lattice L with enough co-primes, equivalently a complete lattice isomorphic as a lattice to the lattice of all closed subsets of some topological space, such that the Scott space Sigma L=(L, sigma(L)) is non-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 3.5. Is there a complete lattice with enough co-primes (i.e., isomorphic to the lattice of all closed subsets of a topological space) that has a non-sober Scott topology?

accepted.question_text: Let B be the complete Boolean algebra of all regular open subsets U of the real line, ordered by inclusion, where regular open means U equals the interior of the closure of U. Is the Scott space Sigma B=(B, sigma(B)) sober?
accepted.context_brief: Regular opens of the real line

evidence.quote: Question 3.6. ([15]) Let B be the complete Boolean algebra of all regular open subsets of the reals line. Is the Scott space ΣB sober?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a complete Boolean algebra B such that its Scott space Sigma B=(B, sigma(B)) is non-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 3.7. Is there a complete Boolean algebra that has a non-sober Scott topology?

accepted.question_text: Characterize all directed complete posets P for which there exists a T0 well-filtered topology tau on the underlying set of P that is compatible with the original order, meaning cl_tau({x})=down x for every x in P. In this setting, well-filtered means that for every open set U and every directed family of nonempty compact saturated subsets, if the intersection of that family is contained in U, then some member of the family is already contained in U.

evidence.quote: Question 4.3. Characterize the well-filtered dcpos.

accepted.question_text: Find necessary and sufficient order-theoretic conditions on a directed complete poset P for its Scott space Sigma P=(P, sigma(P)) to be well-filtered.

evidence.quote: Question 4.5. Find an order characterization for Scott well-filtered dcpos (cf. the first problem below [19, Exercise VII-1.14]).

accepted.question_text: Let P and Q be directed complete posets whose Scott spaces Sigma P and Sigma Q are sober. Must the product dcpo P x Q, ordered coordinatewise, also be Scott sober, meaning that Sigma(P x Q) is sober?

evidence.quote: Question 4.6. Let P, Q be Scott sober dcpos. Must the product P × Q be Scott sober?

accepted.question_text: Let P and Q be well-filtered dcpos, meaning each underlying poset admits a compatible well-filtered topology. Must the product dcpo P x Q be Scott well-filtered, i.e. must the Scott space Sigma(P x Q) be well-filtered?

evidence.quote: Question 4.7. Let P, Q be well-filtered dcpos. Must the product P × Q be Scott well-filtered?

accepted.question_text: Characterize those directed complete posets P such that Sigma P is sober and, for every directed complete poset Q whose Scott space Sigma Q is sober, the product dcpo P x Q is again Scott sober.

evidence.quote: Question 4.8. Characterize those Scott sober dcpos P for which the products P × Q is Scott sober for every Scott sober dcpo Q.

accepted.question_text: Characterize those directed complete posets P such that Sigma P is well-filtered and, for every directed complete poset Q whose Scott space Sigma Q is well-filtered, the product dcpo P x Q is again Scott well-filtered.

evidence.quote: Question 4.9. Characterize those Scott well-filtered dcpos P for which the products P × Q is Scott well-filtered for every Scott well-filtered dcpo Q.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a topological property p of T0 spaces that is weaker than sobriety for general T0 spaces but equivalent to sobriety when restricted to Scott spaces Sigma P of directed complete posets P?

evidence.quote: Question 4.10. Is there a topological property p which is weaker than the sobriety for general T0 topological spaces but equivalent to the sobriety for Scott spaces of dcpos?

accepted.question_text: Is every core compact T0 space a Rudin space? A Rudin space is a T0 space in which every irreducible closed set has the Rudin property, meaning it is a minimal closed set meeting every member of some filtered family of nonempty compact saturated subsets.

evidence.quote: Question 5.15. Is every core compact T0 space a Rudin space?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a full subcategory of Top0 containing Sob, and let X=prod_i X_i be a product of T0 spaces. A subset A of a T0 space is K-determined if every continuous map f from that space to a K-space Y identifies A with the closure of a unique point y_A in Y. If each A_i subset X_i is K-determined, must the product subset prod_i A_i subset X be K-determined?

evidence.quote: Question 5.21. ([49]) Let K be a full subcategory of Top0 containing Sob (in particular, a Keimel-Lawson category) and X = i∈I Xi be the product space of a family {Xi : i ∈ I} of T0 spaces. If each Ai ⊆ Xi (i ∈ I) is K-determined, must the product set i∈I Ai be K-determined?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a full subcategory of Top0 containing Sob. If {X_i}_{i in I} is an arbitrary family of K-determined T0 spaces, is the product space prod_i X_i also K-determined?

evidence.quote: Question 5.22. ([49]) Let K be a full category of Top0 containing Sob (in particular, a Keimel-Lawson category). Is the product space of an arbitrary family of K-determined spaces K-determined?

accepted.question_text: Let X=prod_i X_i be a product of T0 spaces. If each A_i subset X_i is well-filtered determined, meaning it is Topw-determined where Topw is the category of well-filtered spaces, must the product subset prod_i A_i be well-filtered determined?

evidence.quote: Question 5.23. ([51]) Let X = i∈I Xi be the product space of a family {Xi : i ∈ I} of T0 spaces. If each Ai ⊆ Xi (i ∈ I) is well-filtered determined, must the product set i∈I Ai be well-filtered determined?

accepted.question_text: Is the product space of an arbitrary family of well-filtered determined T0 spaces again well-filtered determined, i.e. are all irreducible closed subsets of the product WD sets?

evidence.quote: Question 5.24. ([51]) Is the product space of an arbitrary family of well-filtered determined spaces well-filtered determined?

accepted.question_text: If X is a well-filtered determined T0 space, is its Smyth power space PS(X), the upper Vietoris space on nonempty compact saturated subsets of X, also well-filtered determined?

evidence.quote: Question 6.5. ([51]) Is the Smyth power space PS (X) of a well-filtered determined T0 space X well-filtered determined?

accepted.question_text: For a first-countable well-filtered space X, do the upper Vietoris topology and the Scott topology on K(X), the poset of nonempty compact saturated subsets of X ordered by the Smyth preorder, coincide?

evidence.quote: Question 6.13. ([54]) For a first-countable well-filtered space X, does the upper Vietoris topology and the Scott topology on K(X) coincide?

accepted.question_text: If X is a consonant T0 space, is its Smyth power space PS(X) also consonant? Here consonance means that every Scott-open family of open subsets of X is generated by compact saturated subsets through the filters Phi(K)={U open: K subset U}.

evidence.quote: Question 6.15. ([5]) For a consonant T0 space X, is PS (X) also consonant?

accepted.question_text: If X is a consonant T0 space, is its Hoare power space PH(X), the lower Vietoris space of nonempty closed subsets of X, also consonant?

evidence.quote: Question 6.16. ([5]) For a consonant T0 space X, is PH (X) also consonant?

accepted.question_text: Suppose K is an adequate full subcategory of Top0 that is closed under homeomorphisms. Does the K-reflection functor preserve arbitrary products of T0 spaces; equivalently, for every family {X_i}, is the K-reflection of prod_i X_i homeomorphic to prod_i X_i^K?

evidence.quote: Question 7.14. ([49]) Suppose that K is adequate and closed with respect to homeomorphisms. Does the K-reflection functor preserves arbitrary products of T0 spaces?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a Keimel-Lawson category, meaning a full subcategory of Top0 satisfying the paper's axioms (K1)-(K4), including containing Sob. Does the K-reflection functor preserve arbitrary products of T0 spaces; equivalently, for every family {X_i}, is (prod_i X_i)^K homeomorphic to prod_i X_i^K?

evidence.quote: Question 7.15. ([49]) Let K be a Keimel-Lawson category. Does the K-reflection functor preserves arbitrary products of T0 spaces?

accepted.question_text: Does the d-reflection functor preserve arbitrary products of T0 spaces; equivalently, for every family {X_i}, is the Topd-reflection (prod_i X_i)^d homeomorphic to prod_i X_i^d, where Topd is the category of d-spaces?

evidence.quote: Question 7.16. ([49]) Does the d-reflection functor preserves arbitrary products of T0 spaces?

accepted.question_text: Does the well-filtered reflection functor preserve arbitrary products of T0 spaces; equivalently, for every family {X_i}, is the Topw-reflection (prod_i X_i)^w homeomorphic to prod_i X_i^w, where Topw is the category of well-filtered spaces?

evidence.quote: Question 7.17. ([51]) Does the well-filtered reflection functor preserves arbitrary products of T0 spaces?

accepted.question_text: Let K be an adequate Smyth category, meaning K is adequate and PS(X) is a K-space whenever X is a K-space. If X is a K-determined T0 space, is its Smyth power space PS(X) again K-determined?

evidence.quote: Question 7.20. ([49]) Let K be an adequate Smyth category. Is the Smyth power space PS (X) of a K-determined T0 space X again K-determined?

accepted.question_text: Let Topk be the category of T0 spaces with continuous maps preserving all existing irreducible suprema. Let KBSob be the category of k-bounded sober spaces, where a space is k-bounded sober if every nonempty irreducible closed set whose supremum exists is the closure of a unique point. Is KBSob reflective in Topk?

evidence.quote: Question 7.21. ([37]) Is KBSob reflective in Topk ?

accepted.question_text: Is the product space of an arbitrary family of strong d-spaces again a strong d-space? A T0 space X is strong d if, for every directed set D in the specialization order, point x, and open set U, whenever the intersection over d in D of (up d intersect up x) is contained in U, some single up d intersect up x is already contained in U.

evidence.quote: Question 8.10. Is the product space of an arbitrary family of strong d-spaces again a strong d-space?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a T0 space and Y a strong d-space. Is the function space Top0(X,Y), consisting of continuous maps X to Y and equipped with the pointwise convergence topology, itself a strong d-space?

evidence.quote: Question 8.11. Let X be a T0 space and Y a strong d-space. Is the function space Top0 (X, Y ) equipped with the pointwise convergence topology a strong d-space?

accepted.question_text: Let S-Topd be the full category of strong d-spaces with continuous mappings. Is S-Topd reflective in Top0, the category of T0 spaces and continuous mappings?

evidence.quote: Question 8.12. Is S-Topd reflective in Top0 ?

accepted.question_text: If X is a co-sober T0 space, is its Smyth power space PS(X) again co-sober? Here co-sober means every k-irreducible nonempty compact saturated subset K of X is of the form up k for a unique point k, and PS(X) is the upper Vietoris space on K(X).

evidence.quote: Question 9.4. ([43]) Is the Smyth power space PS (X) of a co-sober space X again co-sober?

accepted.question_text: Let (X,tau) be a co-sober T0 space, and let k:(X,tau)->(X,tau) be continuous. Suppose k is a kernel operator for the specialization order, meaning k(x) lies in cl{x} and k(k(x))=k(x) for every x in X. Is the image subspace (k(X), tau restricted to k(X)) co-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 9.5. Let (X, τ ) be a co-sober space and k : (X, τ ) → (X, τ ) a continuous mapping for which k : X → X is a kernel operator with respect to the specialization order of X, that is, k(x) ∈ cl{x} and k(k(x)) = k(x) for any x ∈ X. Is the subspace (k(X), τ |k(X)) co-sober?

accepted.question_text: Is every retract of a co-sober T0 space again co-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 9.6. Is a retract of a co-sober space co-sober?

accepted.question_text: Is the product space of an arbitrary family of co-sober T0 spaces again co-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 9.7. Is the product space of a family of co-sober spaces co-sober?

accepted.question_text: Let Co-Sob be the category of co-sober spaces with continuous mappings. Is Co-Sob reflective in Top0?

evidence.quote: Question 9.8. Is Co-Sob reflective in Top0 ?

evidence.quote: Question 3.13. ([30]) If L is a meet-continuous dcpo and ΣP is core compact, is ΣP sober?

Extracted explicit Questions 4.3 and 4.5-4.10 on well-filtered dcpos and Scott sober/well-filtered dcpos.
Extracted explicit Questions 5.15 and 5.21-5.24 on Rudin, K-determined, and well-filtered determined spaces.
Extracted explicit Questions 6.5, 6.13, 6.15, and 6.16 on Smyth/Hoare power spaces and consonance.
Extracted explicit Questions 7.14-7.17, 7.20, and 7.21 on reflection functors and Smyth categories.
Extracted explicit Questions 8.10-8.12 on strong d-spaces.
Extracted explicit Questions 9.4-9.8 on co-sober spaces.
Rewrote all accepted numbered source questions into standalone form, inlining definitions from Sections 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 where needed.
Checked extracted numbered questions for near-duplicates; retained distinct source-numbered questions as separate items.
Accepted items have page-numbered primary problem-statement evidence, standalone question text, and solved-status metadata set to false because the source does not mark them solved.

Moved to needs_review because Question 3.14 uses inconsistent symbols P and L that cannot be resolved from local evidence.
